title: Interactive PTCG reasoning simulators

sections.title: Prize-race planning
sections.summary: A deterministic turn timeline shows how attacks per knockout, prizes per knockout and initiative change the shortest projected route to zero prizes.
sections.why_it_matters: The best move can be the move that changes the prize race, not the move with the largest immediate damage number.

sections.title: Damage and knockout thresholds
sections.summary: A simplified damage sandbox exposes existing damage, modifiers, weakness, resistance, remaining HP and hits to knockout.
sections.why_it_matters: Threshold effects can make a small modifier strategically decisive even when average damage changes little.

sections.title: Exact deck-draw odds
sections.summary: A hypergeometric calculator gives the exact probability of drawing zero or more copies of a key card from a 60-card deck.
sections.why_it_matters: Deck ideas should balance consistency against the opportunity cost of each extra copy.

sections.title: Semantic legal-option decisions
sections.summary: An option-scoring and STOP-aware multi-select lab demonstrates temperature, masks, semantic identity and engine-list permutation invariance.
sections.why_it_matters: The submitted policy must score the legal options it receives without treating an arbitrary list index as the meaning of an action.

boundaries: The simulators are educational approximations and do not replace the competition engine.
Damage-effect ordering, card text, legality and terminal outcomes remain engine-authoritative.
Simulator observations are hypothesis prompts, not evaluation evidence or permission to train.
